item.title: Colorful Terminal Output with Jansi
item.description:
Jansi is a Java library for generating and processing ANSI escape sequences. These sequences let a terminal display colors and styles, move the cursor, erase parts of the screen, and perform other terminal operations.

For example, the following bytes mean “use bold red text,” print FAILED, and then restore the terminal’s default attributes:

text 
\u001B[1;31mFAILED\u001B[0m

Writing those codes by hand is difficult to read and easy to get wrong. Jansi provides a fluent Java API for constructing them and terminal-aware streams that can pass through, adapt, or remove them as appropriate.

item.title: Java Logging with SLF4J and Log4j 2
item.description:
SLF4J is a logging API facade. Application code should depend on slf4j-api, while deployment selects one compatible provider such as Log4j 2 or Logback. SLF4J 2 discovers providers through ServiceLoader; retain exactly one. With Log4j 2, log4j-slf4j2-impl adapts SLF4J to Log4j Core. Do not combine it with log4j-to-slf4j, because events then re-enter the facade and form a bridge loop.

java 
private static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(Orders.class);
log.info("Accepted order {}", orderId);
log.warn("Order {} failed validation", orderId, exception);

Parameterized messages defer formatting while the level is disabled. Use an explicit exception argument rather than interpolating a stack trace into text.
